subtopic: Critical Rendering Path, Layout Thrashing and Reflows
question_text:
### Production Incident Scenario:
Production Incident #23: Real User Monitoring (RUM) alerts triggered on the core customer checkout flow due to severe Interaction to Next Paint (INP) degradation and frame dropping in Web Performance, Caching & Rendering Optimization. Profiling reveals frequent 250ms long tasks originating from 'Critical Rendering Path, Layout Thrashing and Reflows'.

### Engineering Challenge:
What is the most effective frontend architecture pattern to bring INP below the 200ms 'Good' threshold for 'Critical Rendering Path, Layout Thrashing and Reflows'?

options.text: Wrap all DOM mutation handlers inside synchronous while-loops until layout computation finishes.
Replace modern reactive state hooks with direct synchronous document.write calls.
Yield execution to the main thread using scheduler.yield() or requestIdleCallback, and defer non-urgent state recalculations via useTransition/web workers.
Disable hardware acceleration and set CSS will-change on all DOM nodes globally.

answer_explanation: Long synchronous JavaScript execution during 'Critical Rendering Path, Layout Thrashing and Reflows' blocks the browser main thread from processing user taps and keystrokes. Decomposing monolithic tasks with scheduler.yield() or React concurrent transitions allows the browser to interleave urgent paint updates, ensuring responsive INP.
reference_solution: Recommended Remediation: Option C.
